messages:
janet-cust: Hi team — we're seeing intermittent stream resets from our integration. Client gets a few event-stream chunks then connection drops with: "HTTP/2 stream 0 RST_STREAM 2". Request ID: r-0b12c34d5e6f7a8b. Region: us-west-2. Started ~2026-03-16T18:00:00Z.

sam-support: Sorry you're hitting this. Can you paste a minimal curl reproduction (redact the key) and the full -v output? Also confirm whether you're going through a proxy / corporate gateway.

janet-cust: attaching what we used in prod (redacted). Behaviour seems the same from our laptop and from a server behind a corp proxy.

```
# our redacted repro
curl -i -N \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --http2 \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1.0","input":"stream test"}' \
  "https://api.redwood.inference/v1/streams/generate"
```

janet-cust: -v shows TLS frames then a chunked 200, a few server-sent events, then the RST_STREAM and connection close. No 4xx/5xx body.

sam-support: thanks. A couple of quick asks so we can escalate:
- run the same curl with `-v --trace-ascii /tmp/curl-trace.txt` and attach that file (captures low-level frames)
- add `-H "X-Request-ID: r-0b12c34d5e6f7a8b"` to the request so we can map logs on our side
- include the exact timestamp window (UTC) when you saw the failure

sam-support: also try this variant which forces streaming behaviour and shows if the client buffers: 

```
curl -i -N --http2 -v \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: r-0b12c34d5e6f7a8b" \
  --no-buffer \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1.0","input":"stream test"}' \
  "https://api.redwood.inference/v1/streams/generate"
```

maya-eng: fyi, when we see RST_STREAM 2 in our infra traces it's usually an upstream connection shutdown (proxy/nginx) or a TLS/ALPN mismatch when clients fall back. A few extra things to test:
- try without proxy (direct internet) and with `--http1.1` to see if HTTP/2 is a factor
- add `-H "Connection: keep-alive" -H "TE: trailers"` — some proxies drop trailers/streaming if TE isn't present
- run `openssl s_client -alpn h2 -connect api.redwood.inference:443` from the same host to confirm ALPN negotiation

janet-cust: will try the trace and the http1.1 test. Quick question — should we include `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`? our client doesn't set that explicitly.

sam-support: you don't need to set Transfer-Encoding manually for this endpoint. The server speaks chunked/event-stream framing appropriately. If you're behind an edge proxy that re-chunks responses, that could cause early resets.

infra-bot: Log bundle available for request r-0b12c34d5e6f7a8b: https://internal-logs.redwood/archives/r-0b12c34d5e6f7a8b (expires in 7d). Found repeated socket error: "write: broken pipe" on worker-14 around 2026-03-16T18:00:12Z.

maya-eng: that broken pipe in the worker is consistent with an upstream client closing the stream unexpectedly. After you run the curl -v --trace, paste the trace and we'll correlate with the bundle. If you can, also paste the `curl --version` output and your OS.

janet-cust: uploaded /tmp/curl-trace.txt and curl-version: curl 8.3.1 (x86_64-pc-linux-gnu) libcurl/8.3.1 OpenSSL/3.1.3 zlib/1.2.11. I also ran `--http1.1` and the stream completed without reset.

sam-support: that's a useful signal — indicates HTTP/2 path involved. Can you retry with `--http2 --no-alpn` (if curl build supports) or try from a different network without the proxy? Also please run with `-H "TE: trailers"` and `-H "Connection: keep-alive"` as maya suggested.

janet-cust: re-ran with TE and Connection headers while forcing --http2, still saw one RST_STREAM 2 in ~10 attempts. From laptop (no proxy) it was clean. From corp proxy it fails.

sam-support: looks like a proxy/network middlebox is the root cause. We'll escalate to infra to add a targeted fallback: automatic downgrade to http/1.1 for streaming requests from that region/account while we coordinate with your network team.

maya-eng: deferring to infra to tweak routing rules. For our internal troubleshooting, we still want the curl -v trace and the request mapping — we have the log bundle link but need the trace file content for the exact TCP/TLS frames.

janet-cust: attaching the trace text inline.

sam-support: got it, thanks. I've opened an internal ticket INC-2026-342 with infra and linked the log bundle and trace. We'll follow up once infra confirms the routing fallback and we validate your repro. :thumbsup:
